claims.text: Formation of chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys at intermediate temperatures below about 1200 K.
The proposed suppression of lattice thermal conductivity is caused by increased phonon scattering from diffuse antiphase boundaries associated with SRO.
The SRO-induced suppression of lattice thermal conductivity diminishes above about 1500 K.
At high temperature, the entropy term in the free-energy barrier diminishes the effective SRO/DAPB strengthening contribution.
Increasing temperature can shift thermal transport from a scattering-dominated regime to an ordering-dominated or thermally activated regime.
MoNbTaW can be modeled with a chemical SRO state equilibrated and fixed at approximately 800 K.
Glide of a screw dislocation through SRO MoNbTaW disrupts local order and creates a DAPB segment.
The cited SRO strengthening mechanism applies in stress regimes where screw-dislocation motion is governed by double-kink nucleation.
DAPBs exist at interfaces between ordered regions and a disordered matrix.
DAPBs scatter phonons because they locally disrupt chemical periodicity.
SRO adds a DAPB enthalpy term to the free energy of kink-pair formation, thereby impeding screw-dislocation motion.
The mechanical strengthening produced by SRO attenuates as temperature increases.
Thermal attenuation of the DAPB free-energy contribution reduces the phonon-scattering cross-section and permits lattice thermal conductivity to recover.
The SRO alloy will have significantly lower thermal conductivity than the RSS baseline from 300 to 1000 K.
The difference in thermal conductivity between SRO and RSS states will approach zero above 1500 K.
Screw-dislocation mobility in simulated SRO and RSS MoNbTaW becomes essentially coincident at 2000 K.
An order-disorder transition near 1100 K is representative of W-Ta-Cr-V-based refractory alloys.
Irradiation-induced ballistic mixing near or above the ODTT can drive SRO parameters toward zero.
Extreme thermal cycling above the ODTT destroys SRO.
The fixed-SRO treatment is restricted to measurement or deformation timescales short enough that the SRO state does not evolve appreciably.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies below an illustrative ODTT of about 1100 K and does not apply after excursions above the ODTT, while the central predicted attenuation and convergence of thermal conductivity are assigned to temperatures above 1500 K. Thus, the high-temperature prediction lies outside the hypothesis's own stated applicability.
